purpose: Teach: 原始/平面/増進/傷害/放火/脅し/蔓延/肝臓

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、原始時代の生活様式の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you covered primitive-era living practices in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, measured observation. Gentle confirmation rather than question. Steady eye contact — the teacher who's genuinely following the student's work, not testing them.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、画家の平面構成理論を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on painters' compositional theory in the plane.
lines.style: Quiet, slightly hesitant start. Straightforward delivery of what he actually studied. A small beat before 'plane' — acknowledging the shift from what she expected.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、健康増進プログラムの効果を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you addressed the effects of health promotion programmes, didn't you?
lines.style: Calm, reflective tone. No accusation — genuine curiosity about the discrepancy. The pause before the question suggests she's cataloguing, not correcting.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、傷害事件の心理学的分析を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I analyzed assault cases from a psychological perspective.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact delivery. Unflinching about the topic shift. No apology in his voice, just clarity. He's used to his own rabbit holes.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 連続放火事件の捜査史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You covered the investigative history of serial arson cases, didn't you?
lines.style: Slightly more engaged now — she's picked up the pattern. Lighter touch. The hint of a smile in her voice, like she's enjoying this puzzle.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、組織犯罪の脅し構造を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — the extortion structures within organized crime networks.
lines.style: Steady, unselfconscious. He's not embarrassed by the drift. Speaks with the same even confidence as before, anchored in what he knows.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、感染症の蔓延要因を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you examined transmission factors in infectious disease outbreaks, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm but patient. The rhythm of the conversation has become almost playful. She's still following his logic, still genuinely asking.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、肝臓病の予防医学を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — preventive medicine approaches to liver disease.
lines.style: Final statement with quiet resolution. A gentle close — he's settled into his answers. Not defensive, just complete.
